newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends higher after rally in July.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends higher after rally in July.

text.p: Soymeal futures ended higher after a short-covering rally in July pulled all months higher in late trade.
"When we made new highs for the day, we went through a lot of stops," said one soy complex trader. "There was a lot of short covering in July."
July rallied up as much as $5.10 per ton at one point before retreating a bit at the close.
In contrast, soyoil futures ended with small to moderate losses after all months made fresh contract lows during the session.
New crop contracts are expected to remain pressured as long as U.S. Midwest weather stays favorable for the new crop.
Supportive factors in Monday's trade included recent news that ADM and some other crushers were cutting back on crush operations.
Traders also continued to watch soyoil export markets because as CBOT soyoil prices sink, the U.S. is becoming more competitive with South America, they said.
July soymeal closed $2.80 higher at $273.70 a ton and other months were up $0.50 to $1.60. July soyoil ended down 0.10 cent a lb at 22.75 cents. Other months were 0.05 to 0.18 cent lower.
Traders were also waiting for crushing data from the U.S. Census Bureau crush report for May.
Analysts expect the report, set for release at 0700 CDT/1200 GMT Tuesday, to show soymeal stocks at between 295,000 to 333,000 tonnes, and soyoil stocks that range from 2.090 to 2.120 billion lbs.
In soymeal trade, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought 400 lots December and Merrill Lynch bought 600 lots July. Smith Barney sold 600 lots August and bought 200 lots July, pit sources said.
In soyoil trade, Cargill bought 200 lots December and 100 lots September, Lind-Waldock bought 500 lots August and Term Commodities sold 200 August and 100 January, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 23,954 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Friday's 25,948.
